Nos Petrus Judocus Vlricus et Johannes fratres de Rosenberch vniuersis, ad quos presens scribtum deueniret, volumus fore notum, quod in tabula, que per dilectam genitricem nostram dominam Ka- therinam de Rosenberch ac nos in modum rose cristalline comparata est, certissime reliquie recondite sunt, que per illustres principes dominum Karolum Romanorum ac Bohemio regem ac per dominum Ludwicum regem Vngarie necnon per venerabües dominos dominum Nycolaum patriarcham Aquilegiensem ac dominum Arnestum archie- piscopum Pragensem donate l'uerunt; qua rum quedam per supradic- torum principum man u s de sepulchris .sanctorum sunt recepte, que dam vero sub bullis domini pape per eosdem principes inuente, quedam vero per abbatis videlicet monasterii sanete Braxedis et abbatem Albanensem ciuitutis Romane, relique vero per honorabiles dominos sacristanos ecclesiarum Prageusis ac Pabenbftrgensis tradite fueruut, quarum nomina inferius recitabuntur. Ich Meinhart der Fleut*) von Weichersdorff vnd ich Vrsula sein hausfraw vnd vnnser baider erben wir verjehen vnd thuen kundt allen den, die disen brieff lesen oder horen lesen die lebend vnnd hernach kunfftigclich sindt, das wir mit gemainem radt vnd bedach tem muet mit willen vnnd gonst aller vnnser frewndt zw der zeit, do wir es wol gethun mochten, vnuerschaidenleich verkauft haben vnnsern Weingarten, der da ligt an dem perg, der da haiset „gelaub wir vnnsern" vnd haisset auch der weingartn allsam, des vier joch sindt, mit sambt dem ackher, der vor dem weingarten leit, als lang der weingart ist an der lenng, vnnd acht klaffter vnd zwo elln nach der brait, vnd ist alles freis aigen, also das man nichts daruon dien- net noch dienen soll weder voithrecht noch perckrecht noch klains vnd gross, dan einen emer weins zw seelgret zw der pfarr zw Weicherstorff, dem man raichen sol den lewten, die zw ostern zw gots disch geen, vnd den sol in nemen, wer zechmaister daselb ist, in dem lesen vor dem weingarten oder in der press. Wir haben in auch geben ainen freien wege vnd ein freye strassen mittenn von dem weingarten vbor ale äcker vnc/Л auf die lanndstrasse in vnd allen lewten, die da zw schaffen habend, also das ein wagen freilich da.geen mag vnd ein knecht daneben vnd auch ein wagen dem ann- dern geweichen mag, ob sein not geschäch, sy sein geseet oder nicht. Krumau. — Die Brüder Peter, Jodok, Ulrich und Johann von Rosenberg schenken der Kirche des heiligen Nikolaus in Rosenberg den ganzen Getreidezehent vom Mauthof. Nos Petrus Judocus Vlricus et Johannes fratres de Rosenberch recognoscimus et ad vniuersorum noticiam cupimus peruenire, quod bona et libera voluntate ducti maturoque consilio desuper prehabito decimam plenam et integram de quadruplici grano, tantum scilicet ') Soll heissen Preheutag. 115 siligneo triticeo ordeaceo et auenatico de omnibus, que in agris seu in ortis ad curiam nostram in Mutam pertinentibus proueniunt, ad ecclesiam in Rozeuberch fundatam in honore sancti Nicolai confes sons, ad quam ipsa curia riostra predicta in iure spirituali et sacra- mentis pertinet ab antiquo, siue plebano eiusdem ecclesie disposui- uriis et statuimus dandam perpetue et soluendam per nos seu eciam alios nostros quoscumque successores, addicientes, quod si ipsa nostra sepedicta curia vna cum agris ad ipsam spectautibus per nos aut heredes nostros alio venderetur cuicumque, vel alio quocumque modo ipsam curiam locare contingat, semper plena decima de omni bus, ut supradictum est, ad sepedictam ecclesiam in Rozenberch siue plebano eiusdem ecclesie, quicumque fuerit, persolui debet atque dari integraliter et ex toto contradictione qualibet procul muta. Item eidem sepiusfate ecclesie in Rozenberch seu plebano eiusdem ecc lesie, qui pro tempore fuerit, medium talentum denariorum Wien- nensium damus et donamus expresse in judicialibus denariis de iu- dicio Rozenbergensi perpetuis temporibus percipiendum deputantes Ipse quoque plebanus, qui pro tune extiterit, ibidem in capella caslrj nostri Rozenberch in honore sancti Johannis apostoli et ewangeliste fundata diuinum officium cum vna missa singulis feriis sextis consi- deratis premissis beneficiis debebit et tenebitur procurare. In casu tamen, vbi feria sexta comode missa non possit inibi celebrari, tune alio quocunque vno die omni septimana in prefata capella ex proui- sione prefati plebani officium diuinum vnius misse in perpetuum te- neantur. Ne autem tempore succedente hec nostra bona et ¡usía donationis constitucio et salubris ocdinatio per maliciam seu violen- ciam aliquorum valeat. aliquatenus violari in dispendium animarum ipsorum et in dampnacionem sempiternam, presentes litteras scribi et sigillorum nostrorum munimine duximus roborari in testimonium et robur perpetue valiturum. entries.english:
1354, 5 October, Krumau. — Peter, Jodok, Ulrich, and Johann, brothers von Rosenberg, and Tobias von Bechin testify that the relics kept in a reliquary panel acquired by Katherine von Rosenberg, the mother of the aforesaid brothers, were given to them by Emperor Charles IV, King Ludwig I of Hungary, the Patriarch Nikolaus of Aquileia, and Archbishop Arnest of Prague. 1356, 6 January, undated place. — Meinhart der Fleut von Weikersdorf and his wife sell a vineyard to Abbot Albrecht and the community of Hohenfurt Monastery for 59 pounds of Viennese pennies. 1356, 21 March, Krumau. — The brothers Peter, Jodok, Ulrich, and Johann von Rosenberg give the entire grain tithe from the Mauthof to the Church of St Nicholas in Rosenberg.

CIV. We, Peter, Jodok, Ulrich, and Johann, brothers von Rosenberg, make known to all to whom this present writing may come that the panel, which was acquired in the form of a crystal rose by our beloved mother, Lady Katherine von Rosenberg, and by us, certainly contains relics given by the illustrious princes Lord Charles, King of the Romans and Bohemia, and Lord Ludwig, King of Hungary, and by the venerable lords Lord Nikolaus, Patriarch of Aquileia, and Lord Arnest, Archbishop of Prague. Some of these relics were received by the hands of the aforesaid princes from the tombs of saints; others were found by those same princes under the seals of the lord pope; some were given by the abbots of the monastery of St Praxedis and of St Alban in the city of Rome; and others were delivered by the honorable sacristans of the churches of Prague and Pabenbftrg. Their names are listed below. First, in the cross held by the angel standing above the panel, there is a part of the most holy table at which the Lord ate with his disciples at the Last Supper. Also a tooth of St John the Baptist, held by the image of that saint standing above the panel; a tooth of St Wenceslas, likewise held in the hand of his image; a stone from the Lord’s tomb; and a part of the mantle of blessed Elizabeth, in which, while pregnant, she carried her son St John the Baptist and greeted the Mother of God. Also relics of St Peter the Apostle; St John the Baptist; St Andrew, St Paul, St James the Greater, St Bartholomew, St Matthias the Apostle, St Mark the Evangelist, and St Luke the Evangelist; and a part of St Peter’s tunic. Also relics of St Wenceslas, St Vitus, St Adalbert, the Five Holy Brothers of Bolesław, St Ludmila the martyr, St Procopius the confessor, and St Stanislaus; and a part of St Adalbert’s tunic. Also relics of St George the martyr, St Calixtus, St Sebastian, St Sergius and St Bacchus, St Clement, St Januarius, the Ten Thousand Martyrs, St Colman, St Gervasius, St Erasmus, St Cletus and St Daria the martyrs, St Alban the martyr, St Meinrad the martyr, St Blaise, St Gereon, St Dionysius, St Vincent, St Pudentius, and St Christopher; and a part of the cross of St Andrew the Apostle. Also relics of St Martin, St Nicholas, an arm of St Thomas Aquinas, St Pope Sylvester, St Gall, St Othmar, St Anthony of the Friars Minor, St Augustine, St Onuphrius, St Stephen King of Hungary, St Henry the Emperor, St Nicasius, and St Vitus of Siena. Also a stone from the tomb of the Mother of God; relics of St Anne, her mother; St Mary Magdalene, St Helena, St Agatha, St Lucy, St Dorothy, St Elizabeth of Marburg, St Cunigunde, St Afra, St Hedwig, St Eulalia, St Candida, St Gene, St Petronilla, St Juliana, St Thecla, St Euphemia, the Eleven Thousand Virgins, St Walpurga the virgin, and St Hermator the confessor. So that the devotion of the faithful to these holy relics may increase more greatly and certainly, we, Peter von Rosenberg, canon of the Church of Prague, and the aforesaid brothers Jodok, Ulrich, and Johann von Rosenberg, as well as Tobias von Bechin, called de Kempnycz, affirm and attest on the truth of our faith that the aforesaid relics were given by the aforesaid lords. In witness thereof we have caused our seals to be attached to these presents. Given at Krumau in the year of the Lord 1354, on the octave of the glorious martyr St Wenceslas.

Five seals hang from green and red silk cords. (a) Seal in red wax: a man in a long flowing robe, short mantle, and halo, holding a book in his right hand and a shield bearing a rose in his left; an identical shield appears to the right of the seal. Inscription: “Seal of Peter von Rosenberg, canon of Prague”; compare LXXXVIII. (b) Small counterseal in red wax, a five-petalled rose with a capital M between each pair of petals; inscription: “Seal of Peter von Rosenberg.” (c) Small seal in red wax: a shield with a rose, surmounted by a helmet also bearing a rose; inscription: “Seal of Jodok von Rosenberg.” Its counterseal, nearly as large, shows a bearded man’s head in an antique helmet; inscription: “Seal of Jodok von Rosenberg.” (d) Small seal in white wax: a shield with a rose, surmounted by a helmet decorated with roses; inscription: “Seal of Ulrich von Rosenberg.” (e) Small seal in white wax: a shield with a rose, above it a helmet whose crest is also a rose; inscription: “Seal of Johann von Rosenberg.” (The fifth seal is small, in white wax, and shows a shield with a horseshoe from which an arrowhead emerges, with a cross above the shield; inscription: “Seal of Tobias von Bechin.”)

CV. 1356, 6 January, undated place. — Meinhart der Fleut von Weikersdorf and his wife Ursula sell a vineyard to Abbot Albrecht and the community of Hohenfurt Monastery for 59 pounds of Viennese pennies. I, Meinhart der Fleut of Weichersdorff, and I, Ursula his wife, and our heirs together acknowledge and make known to all, living now or in future, who read or hear this charter, that with common counsel and considered mind, with the consent and goodwill of all our friends at the time when we could properly do so, we have jointly sold our vineyard, lying on the hill called “Gelaub wir unsern,” also called the Allsam vineyard, comprising four yokes, together with the field lying before the vineyard, extending along its length and measuring eight fathoms and two ells in width. All of it is freehold, owing no dues, whether vogt-right, vineyard-right, minor or major dues, except one bucket of wine for the soul’s offering at the parish church of Weichersdorff, to be given to those who receive communion at Easter, and collected by the churchwarden there during the vintage before the vineyard or at the press. We have also granted them a free way and road from the vineyard, across all the fields, to the highway, for all who have business there, so that a wagon may pass freely, with a servant beside it, and one wagon may pass another if necessary, whether the land is sown or not. We have lawfully and rightly sold and conveyed the aforesaid vineyard, field, and road, together with all the uses and rights that have come down from old custom and that we have held in ownership, for fifty-nine pounds of Viennese pennies, which we have received in full, to the honorable Lord Abbot Albrecht and the community of lords of Hohenfurt Monastery, to possess freely and without encumbrance, and to do with them whatever benefits them—sell, pledge, or give them to whomever they wish—without dispute or hindrance. For further security, I, the aforesaid Meinhart der Fleut of Weichersdorff, and I, Ursula his wife, and our heirs jointly warrant and defend the aforesaid vineyard, field, and way to the honorable Lord Abbot Albrecht and the community of Hohenfurt Monastery against every claim, as the law of freehold and the law of the land of Austria require. If they suffer a legal claim or dispute concerning that vineyard, field, or way, we shall make good all their losses and compensate them for all their trouble and damage. They shall have this assurance on our good faith and against all our property, wherever in the land of Austria or elsewhere we may have it, whether we are alive or dead. So that this sale and agreement may henceforth remain firm and unbroken, we give them this charter as true evidence and lasting confirmation, sealed with my own seal and the attached seals of Fridrich der Pluemen of Wisendorff, Conrad der Pluemen of Starendwerd, and Dietmar der Pluemen of Weichersdorff, whom I earnestly asked to witness the transaction along with other honorable people. The charter was given after Christ’s birth in the year 1356, on “Piehentag” [sic; intended: Preheutag]. From a copy authenticated by Lord Jobst von Rosenberg, dated Krumau, Monday after the Nativity of Mary, 1535; compare XCVIII.

CVI. 1356, 21 March, Krumau. — The brothers Peter, Jodok, Ulrich, and Johann von Rosenberg give the entire grain tithe from the Mauthof to the Church of St Nicholas in Rosenberg. We, Peter, Jodok, Ulrich, and Johann, brothers von Rosenberg, acknowledge and wish to make known to all that, moved by good will and after mature deliberation, we have decreed and established that the full and entire tithe of four kinds of grain—namely rye, wheat, barley, and oats—from all that is produced in the fields or gardens belonging to our manor at Mauth shall be given perpetually to the Church of St Nicholas founded at Rosenberg, to which the aforesaid manor has from of old belonged in spiritual jurisdiction and in the sacraments, or to its parish priest. We decree that it shall be paid perpetually by us or by any of our successors. We add that if we or our heirs sell that manor, together with its fields, to anyone, or lease it in any other way, the full tithe of all the aforesaid produce must always be paid in full to the said Church of Rosenberg or its priest, whoever he may be, without any objection. We also expressly give to the same church, or its priest for the time being, half a talent of Viennese pennies from the judicial revenues of the Rosenberg court, to be received in perpetuity. The priest then serving there shall also be required, in consideration of these benefits, to conduct divine service with one mass every Friday in the chapel founded in honor of St John the Apostle and Evangelist in our castle of Rosenberg. If a mass cannot conveniently be celebrated there on Friday, then, at the priest’s discretion, divine service with one mass shall be held in that chapel on another day each week. Lest in time to come this good and just act of donation and wholesome ordinance be violated by anyone’s malice or force, to the harm of their souls and their eternal damnation, we have caused these letters to be written and strengthened with the protection of our seals, as enduring witness and confirmation. Given at Krumau in the year of the Lord 1356, on the Monday after the Sunday on which “Reminiscere” is sung. The four familiar small seals of the Rosenberg brothers, all here in red wax and described above under CIV, hang from parchment strips.
